summary: Defines ConnectionProtocol[C], the runtime-checkable generic protocol every connection implements, parameterised by the native client type. It requires connect() returning Self, idempotent disconnect(), client and is_connected properties, and context-manager methods. The docstring fixes lifecycle rules: disconnect cleans up partial acquisition and is idempotent after failure, connect may reopen, context-body errors stay primary over cleanup errors, and decorator connections exclusively own their children.
key_classes: ConnectionProtocol[C] — runtime-checkable lifecycle protocol (connect/disconnect/client/is_connected/__enter__/__exit__) over a covariant native client type C
extension_points: Implement ConnectionProtocol to add a new connection type (leaf over a native client, or decorator wrapping another connection like SFTPConnection/TunnelledConnection); the facade and backends accept any conforming object
lifecycle_notes: disconnect() must release all owned resources, including partially acquired ones, and be safe to call repeatedly even after a failed close
connect() may reopen a connection; this differs from StorageFacade.close(), which is terminal
Decorator connections exclusively own their inner connection and must close it
create_connection() is typed as returning ConnectionProtocol[Any] because the client type depends on the runtime provider (docs/typing.md)
documentation_hooks: Architecture page: leaf vs decorator connections and ownership
Connection lifetime section (README) and how it differs from facade lifetime
risks: runtime_checkable isinstance checks only verify attribute presence, not the documented idempotence and ownership semantics; conformance depends on per-connection tests

evidence.detail: Connections table lists leaf and decorator connections
